correctness.rationale: With X=KN and X³=0, the product is B=I+aN+b₂N², a=K(1−2t), b₂=K²(t²−2t). A, q_t(A) and B are upper triangular with diagonal one. Uniform positivity for complex Rayleigh quotients is equivalent to positive definiteness of the real symmetric part. I eliminated the middle coordinate using its unit diagonal; the remaining 2×2 Schur complement has eigenvalues 1−b₂/2 and 1+(b₂−a²)/2. Now a²−b₂=K² f(t), f(t)=1−2t+3t²=2/3+3(t−1/3)², and b₂<K² f(t) for K>0. Thus the exact safety interval for each slope is K² f(t)<2, also valid at K=0. Its maximal range is K<√3 for the unique t=1/3; t=1/2 gives K<√(8/3). To independently check the witness, the unnormalized real vector (1,y,1) has quadratic form (y+a)²+2−K² f(t), with a real zero whenever K≥√3, for every slope. Applying q_t(A)⁻¹ to this vector and starting with q_t(A)b realizes the zero in H₁ after normalization. At the optimal endpoint v=(1,−1/√3,1) comes from the stated input b=(1,0,1). In the truncated polynomial ring the square of I−X/2+3X²/8 is I−X+X² and multiplication by I+X gives I; in size two already X²=0 and the linear Taylor polynomial works for all K. The finding concerns exact real normalized affine slopes and one-step left Arnoldi. Above the threshold, a failing real input exists for each slope; not every input fails. I inspected the supplied checker without executing it; these conclusions are algebraic.

evidence: Carden–Embree treat the bare shift and bounds on real parts of separate Ritz values; §3 gives the deeper joint characterization. Frommer et al.'s spectral analysis in §3.2 is restricted to Hermitian positive-definite A, and §5 states general right-half-plane field-of-values control for Ritz values. Tichý–Liesen–Faber use an affine polynomial on a Jordan block for ideal GMRES norm bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The standard Hermitian-part or field-of-values criterion applies but does not give the sharp signs uniformly along the affine preconditioning curve; the Jordan GMRES theorem optimizes a different norm under a different polynomial normalization.
searches: Carden–Embree §§1, 2.2 and 3 on the 3×3 Jordan block

evidence: The Ritz-pair theorem can be used to pose the same left-support optimization over its feasible set, but has no slope family or optimization along the coefficients (K(1−2t),K²(t²−2t)). The indexed joint radius bounds magnitudes in aggregate, not their signed linear combination in this direction. The branch condition spec(q(A))⊂ℂ⁺ is satisfied even at the singular examples.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The sharp barrier is not a direct specialization of a known bound or a tabulated number. Extracting it from the prior joint-set description would still require solving an extremum over Ritz pairs and then over slopes, as well as locating a real witness. The elementary Schur complement yields that new optimization and shows exactly which quantifiers hold. Do not treat the degree-two Taylor identity as an independent novelty claim.

evidence: Frommer et al. use exactly c=q(A)b and the preconditioned operator q(A)²A. Carden–Embree identify v*Nv=−(θ₁+θ₂) and v*N²v=θ₁θ₂ for the two Ritz values of N on v⊥; their Proposition 3.1 characterizes feasible pairs by a cubic root condition, with a special case at zero product.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The one-step Rayleigh quotient of I+aN+b₂N² is exactly 1−a(θ₁+θ₂)+b₂θ₁θ₂ in this formulation. Thus joint moment feasibility and its connection to Ritz pairs are prior, not a new result. It remains to take a directional extremum along the slope-dependent coefficients and optimize the resulting safety interval, not simply to test a given pair.

originality.rationale: Credit the optimized λ=1 Jordan-family obstruction for left inverse-square-root Arnoldi: the sharp uniform threshold, the optimizer and the zero compression for some real input at every slope at and above the threshold. The Arnoldi method and branch condition are established, the joint geometry of the first two Jordan powers has a prior exact characterization through two Ritz values, and degree-two Taylor exactness is routine nilpotent calculus. The inspected prior results do not supply the optimization over this preconditioning curve.
residual_risks: The bounded review does not exclude unindexed computations of the same optimum or a stronger directed-support theorem. The 2021 stability paper was not inspected in full; this is not evidence of no overlap.

value.rationale: This is the minimal Jordan dimension where first-order Taylor exactness fails, and left inverse-square-root Arnoldi is a previously motivated numerical method that actually needs nonsingular compressions. The example excludes every real affine slope past a sharp point despite an innocuous preconditioner spectrum, rather than just noting that eigenvalues may misrepresent the field of values. The sharp comparison to the standard Taylor slope and the explicit singular input make the obstruction usable as a benchmark.
